sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Santa Cruz County, Arizona?
sections.html:
In Santa Cruz County the Assessor values property and the Treasurer collects the tax. The Treasurer’s office is at 2150 N. Congress Drive, Room 104, in Nogales, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Mail goes to PO Box 1150, Nogales, AZ 85628, and checks are made out to the Santa Cruz County Treasurer. The Assessor controls value, legal class, exemptions and the mailing address printed on your bill.

Santa Cruz is the smallest county in Arizona by area, with 1,238 square miles, and it sits on the Mexican border. It was formed on March 15, 1899 out of Pima County and takes its name from the Santa Cruz River. Nogales is the county seat and the only city, Patagonia is the only incorporated town, and Rio Rico, Tubac, Sonoita and Amado are among the unincorporated communities. Two sellers in the same county can therefore deal with the same offices while living in very different places, from a border city lot in Nogales to a ranch parcel near Elgin.

Your bill adds up the rates of every jurisdiction that taxes your parcel: the county, your school district, your fire district and other special districts. The Treasurer explains that primary taxes pay operating costs and secondary taxes pay for special districts, bonds and voter-approved overrides. Primary tax is limited value times the assessment ratio times the primary rate divided by $100, and secondary tax follows the same pattern. Owner-occupied homes also get a State Aid to Education credit against the school primary tax, and a countywide Fire District Assistance tax under ARS 48-807 appears on every taxable parcel.

sections.h2: When are Santa Cruz County property taxes due and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
Bills above $100 split into two installments. The first is due October 1 and delinquent if postmarked or received after 5:00 p.m. on November 1. The second is due March 1 and delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on May 1. A bill of $100 or less is due with the first installment. If you pay both installments in full before 5:00 p.m. on December 31, the interest on the first installment is waived. Statements for the current year go out in mid-September with a coupon for each installment, and that is the only statement you receive unless you fall behind.

Once a deadline passes, interest starts at 16 percent a year, prorated monthly at 1.333 percent whether you pay on the first or last day of the month. A $5 penalty applies to taxes still unpaid when January arrives. The county also warns that partial payment of delinquent tax liens is not allowed, so the minimum it accepts is the tax, interest and fees for a delinquent installment. For the date today, November 15, 2026, the first installment is already delinquent and the second comes due March 1, 2027.

sections.h2: What do the Santa Cruz County numbers look like?
sections.html:
These county figures come from the Census Bureau.

  • Population estimated at 50,020 on July 1, 2025, up 4.9 percent from April 2020.
  • 20,135 housing units, with 353 building permits in 2025.
  • 69.3 percent owner-occupied housing, and a median owner-occupied home value of $233,000 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Median household income of $55,217 and a 24.2 minute mean commute.
  • Median gross rent of $829.

Agriculture here leans on forage, hay and cattle, and the county has three border crossings, all in Nogales. A seller whose house is valued near $233,000 will see a bill built on the limited value, not on that headline figure, so read your own notice.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Santa Cruz County property tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay online, by phone, by mail or in person. The county’s card vendor, Point&Pay, charges $3.95 on debit cards, 2.5 percent on credit card payments over $100 and $2.00 on credit payments below that. An electronic check costs $2.50. The Treasurer receives none of this and is barred by law from charging a processing fee. Allow three to four business days for an online payment to post. Mailed payments should be personal checks, cashier’s checks or money orders, never cash.

To see what you owe for the current year, search the parcel on the county’s property information site and open the taxes tab. For prior years, call the Treasurer at 520-375-7580, because extra charges may not show on the online tab. If you have a mortgage, the Treasurer supplies tax statements to mortgage and tax service companies on request, and you may also get an information statement as a courtesy. The Treasurer has also posted a notice that some bills carry installment amounts that need correcting while the full-year amount is right, so check the posted parcel list if your halves look odd.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Santa Cruz County valuation?
sections.html:
File a Petition for Review of Real Property Valuation, Form 82130, with the Assessor. The Assessor mails notices of valuation by March 1, and state law gives you 60 days from the mailing date. The county FAQ points to the period from March 1 through April 29, and petitions are available at the Assessor’s office. Under ARS 42-16051, your petition must give your opinion of full cash value and back it with the income, market or cost approach.

The Assessor’s office also handles mailing address changes, so ask them to update it when you sell. The Assessor’s number is 520-375-8030. If the Assessor denies your petition, the next step is the County Board of Equalization, then court, within the deadlines printed on the decision.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for a Santa Cruz County property tax exemption?
sections.html:
The county lists exemptions for qualifying widows, widowers and disabled persons. You must apply each year between January 1 and the last working day of February, and first-time applicants must apply in person. Someone holding a power of attorney may file for another person with a copy of the power of attorney and photo ID. Each exemption has its own qualifications, so call the Assessor at 520-375-8030. State law also covers disabled veterans in ARS 42-11111.

The statute lists conveying title to another owner as an event that ends the exemption, so a seller should tell the Assessor after closing. A person who moves to a new primary residence has 60 days to file a transfer form with the assessor in that home’s county.

sections.h2: What happens when Santa Cruz County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The county sells a lien for the unpaid tax at its delinquent tax lien sale, which it holds in February. The 2026 sale was held online on February 10, 2026. Investors bid the interest rate down from 16 percent in 1 percent steps, and a zero percent bid is allowed. The county says that after three years from the sale date, the lien purchaser can foreclose and acquire the property. The county treats this as a sale of the lien and not of the home.

A seller should settle the tax and any lien before closing. Call the Treasurer for a payoff figure, using 520-375-7980 for lien questions and 520-375-7580 for prior-year balances, and give it to the title or escrow company.

sections.h2: What should I do about taxes when selling a Santa Cruz County house?
sections.html:
• Pull the current balance from the parcel search and call the Treasurer for earlier years.
  • Ask whether either installment is open and whether any parcel interest has accrued.
  • Ask the Assessor to change the mailing address and cancel any exemption once title passes.

A house in Nogales, Rio Rico or Patagonia is taxed by the same county office, though the district rates that make up the bill differ by address.

faqs.q: When are Santa Cruz County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first installment is due October 1 and becomes delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1. The second is due March 1 and becomes delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on May 1. Bills of $100 or less are due with the first installment.

faqs.q: Can I avoid interest on the first installment?
faqs.a: Yes, if you pay the total tax for the year, both installments, before 5:00 p.m. on December 31. The county waives interest on the first installment in that case.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for late property tax in Santa Cruz County?
faqs.a: Interest runs at 16 percent a year, prorated at 1.333 percent a month, and a $5 penalty is added for taxes unpaid when January arrives. Unpaid taxes can be sold as a lien at the February tax lien sale.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in person in Santa Cruz County?
faqs.a: At the Treasurer’s office, 2150 N. Congress Drive, Room 104, Nogales, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. You may also mail a check to PO Box 1150, Nogales, AZ 85628, or pay online or by phone with the vendor’s fees.

faqs.q: Can a veteran get a property tax exemption in Santa Cruz County?
faqs.a: State law in ARS 42-11111 provides exemptions for veterans with qualifying disability ratings. Ask the Santa Cruz County Assessor at 520-375-8030 whether you qualify and how to apply, and note that the county’s exemption filing window runs from January 1 to the last working day of February.
